5. annotated historical newspaper digitization and research platform
6. data journalism tutorial and project showcase hub
7. editorial writing craft masterclass and feedback site
8. fact-checking workflow guide and newsroom practice tool
9. long-form narrative reading room with author annotations
10. media literacy curriculum portal for classroom educators
11. photojournalism ethics and technique learning library
12. economics concepts explainer series with curated reading lists
13. climate reporting deep-dive explainer and resource portal
14. podcast transcript library with structured study guides
15. documentary companion learning and discussion resource site

20. technology ethics explainer and case study repository
21. health journalism verification guide and literacy resource

27. multimedia storytelling technique showcase and tutorial library
28. expert interview archive with curated topic learning paths
29. cross-border investigative reporting resource and methodology library

## Hard requirements
1. Output a JSON array of EXACTLY 30 new topic strings, in English.
2. Each topic = a concrete, buildable product/site idea, 4-12 words. Not a generic feature name.
3. CRITICAL — in-scene differentiation: every new topic must be a genuinely different
   sub-niche or use-case from EVERY existing topic listed above. Do NOT produce
   paraphrases, synonyms, renamings, or minor variations. Example: if "freelance
   invoice tracker" already exists, do NOT emit "invoice management tool for
   freelancers". If an idea overlaps in concept with any existing topic, discard it
   and find a different angle (different audience, sub-domain, mechanic, or context).
4. The 30 new topics must also be clearly distinct from each other.

6. Lean web-native: e.g. "open-source contributor leaderboard site", not a phone-only idea.
7. Output pure JSON — a single array of strings. No markdown fences, no commentary.

Return ONLY the JSON array of 30 strings.
